actions.name: Review surgical operative note
actions.result: Right total knee arthroplasty performed 6 weeks ago (cemented, posterior-stabilized implant) for end-stage osteoarthritis. No intraoperative complications. Standard posterior approach. Weight-bearing as tolerated per surgeon postoperatively.

actions.name: Review home exercise log in chart
actions.result: Log shows exercise sessions completed on 9 of the last 28 days, with no entries at all in the last 5 days. Entries that are present are mostly quad sets and ankle pumps; no bending/flexion exercises logged in the last 3 weeks.

actions.name: Vital signs (patient home BP cuff and pulse ox)
actions.result: BP 128/78 mmHg, HR 76 bpm regular, SpO2 98% on room air, temp 97.9°F (36.6°C) reported by patient thermometer. No fever.

actions.name: Camera inspection of surgical incision and knee
actions.result: Well-healed, non-erythematous linear incision over anterior right knee, no drainage, no increased local warmth reported by patient on self-palpation. Mild residual swelling of the knee visible compared to left side.

actions.name: Guided active knee flexion with goniometer app (patient self-measures on camera)
actions.result: Active knee flexion right knee measures 85 degrees; left (unaffected) knee flexion 135 degrees.

actions.name: Guided active/passive knee extension with goniometer app
actions.result: Right knee lacks 10 degrees of full extension (terminal extension to -10 degrees); left knee extends fully to 0 degrees.

actions.name: Calf inspection and self-palpation for DVT screening
actions.result: Calf is soft, symmetric to left, no tenderness reported, no calf swelling, no Homans' sign elicited by guided self-palpation. No visible redness.

actions.name: Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, guided via video with walker
actions.result: 22 seconds to rise from chair, walk 3 meters, turn, return, and sit, using front-wheeled walker. Movements appear cautious and guarded, especially during turning.

actions.name: Guided quadriceps strength screen (sit-to-stand repetitions and seated knee extension against gravity, patient-performed on camera)
actions.result: Patient completes 5 sit-to-stands in 15 seconds using arms to push off; seated active knee extension right leg shows visible quadriceps lag of approximately 10 degrees compared to left.

actions.name: Pain rating with numeric scale (current, with activity, at rest)
actions.result: Pain at rest 2/10; pain during knee flexion stretching exercises 6/10 at end-range; pain resolves to 2/10 within 10 minutes after stopping. No night pain at rest.

actions.name: Review current medication list
actions.result: Oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg, 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain; acetaminophen 650 mg as needed; patient reports taking pain tablet after exercise sessions, not before.

actions.name: Patient self-report functional checklist (stairs, floor transfers, walker use)
actions.result: Uses walker for all indoor and outdoor ambulation; requires two hands on rail and leads with left leg for all stairs; unable to kneel or get up from floor without assistance.

actions.name: Visual gait assessment via camera (short walk with walker)
actions.result: Antalgic gait pattern with shortened stance time on right, reduced right knee flexion during swing phase, forward trunk lean, and reliance on walker for stability during turns.

actions.name: Review prior PT evaluation note (postoperative week 2)
actions.result: At 2 weeks post-op: AROM 0-70 degrees flexion, full extension achieved passively; incision clean/dry/intact with staples removed. Independent with walker for short household distances. TUG deferred (patient fatigued easily). Pain 4/10 with exercise, 1/10 at rest. Home exercise program issued including flexion and extension stretches, quad sets, heel slides, ankle pumps. A linked flexion ROM trend chart (week 2 through week 6) is also available in the record.

artifacts.title: Operative Report - Right Total Knee Arthroplasty
artifacts.author: Dr. Allen Reyes, Orthopedic Surgery
artifacts.body:
PROCEDURE: Right total knee arthroplasty, cemented posterior-stabilized implant.
INDICATION: End-stage osteoarthritis, right knee, failed conservative management.
FINDINGS: Severe tricompartmental cartilage loss, osteophytes removed, patella resurfaced.
COMPLICATIONS: None.
POSTOP ORDERS: Weight-bearing as tolerated with assistive device. Physical therapy to begin postoperative day 1. Goals: knee flexion 110-120 degrees by 6 weeks, full extension, independent ambulation.

artifacts.title: PT Initial Evaluation - Postoperative Week 2
artifacts.author: Physical Therapy
artifacts.body:
S: Patient reports pain 4/10 with exercise, 1/10 at rest. Using front-wheeled walker for all mobility.
O: AROM right knee 0-70 degrees (flexion), full extension achieved passively. Incision clean, dry, intact with staples removed. Independent with walker for short household distances. TUG deferred, patient fatigued easily.
A: Expected postoperative stiffness and quadriceps weakness, on track at 2 weeks but will need close monitoring of ROM progression.
P: Progress HEP to include seated heel slides, prone hangs for extension, quad sets, straight leg raises as tolerated. Follow up in 2 weeks to reassess ROM and gait.

facts.says: My daughter comes by twice a week to help with the shopping and whatnot.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient states she does her home exercises religiously every single day without missing any.
mismatches.recordEvidence: The home exercise adherence log shows entries on only 9 of the last 28 days, with zero entries in the most recent 5 days and no flexion/bending exercises logged in the last 3 weeks.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Self-reported adherence often overestimates actual engagement; cross-checking objective logs is essential before attributing poor outcomes solely to tissue factors, and creates an opening to explore barriers like fear-avoidance non-judgmentally.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient reports taking her pain medication after exercising, once pain has already started.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Medication list confirms oxycodone-acetaminophen is prescribed as needed for pain and the patient's own timing report (post-exercise dosing) is inconsistent with best practice of premedicating 30-45 minutes before therapy to allow adequate analgesia during painful stretching, contributing to exercise avoidance.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Timing of PRN analgesia relative to therapeutic activity significantly affects exercise tolerance and adherence; PT should counsel on premedication timing within scope, coordinating with the prescribing provider as needed.

objectives.text: Identify arthrogenic knee stiffness (flexion and extension deficits) as the primary impairment limiting function 6 weeks post-TKA and distinguish expected postoperative stiffness from red-flag complications (infection, DVT).

Uncover the gap between self-reported exercise adherence and objective adherence data (via chart review alone shows the 'what'), and separately explore through interview the underlying fear-avoidance belief and misunderstanding driving avoidance of flexion exercises (the 'why', which requires asking directly rather than chart review).
Perform and interpret objective functional measures (goniometry, Timed Up and Go, quadriceps strength screen, gait observation) appropriate for a telehealth progress re-evaluation.
Recognize modifiable adherence barriers (pillow positioning promoting extension contracture, suboptimal analgesic timing) and formulate patient-centered education addressing each.
Screen for postoperative red flags (infection, DVT, wound issues) via guided remote exam and determine these are absent, remaining within PT scope rather than escalating unnecessarily.

Establish patient-centered, meaningful functional goals (walking without walker for wedding in 2 months, kneeling in church) and construct a plan of care with appropriate exercise progression and home program revision.

patient.name: Margaret "Peggy" O'Connell
patient.appearance: A silver-haired woman of average build appears seated in a cozy living room with floral curtains and a rosary visible hanging on a nearby lamp. She wears a cardigan over a blouse, has her front-wheeled walker parked beside her chair, and her face shows a mix of warmth and visible worry as she speaks.

persona.personality: Talkative, warm, somewhat anxious, eager to please and to be seen as a 'good patient' who follows instructions.
persona.communicationStyle: Chatty and detailed, often goes on tangents about family or neighbours before circling back to the question; responds well to clear, logical explanations and reassurance.
persona.emotionalState: Worried about falling behind schedule and about disappointing her family by using a walker at the wedding; mildly embarrassed when gently confronted with the exercise log discrepancy.
persona.background: Worked over 30 years as a bookkeeper for a local hardware store before retiring. Widowed four years ago, lives alone in a two-story house in Buffalo where she raised three children. Active in her parish, enjoys baking for church fundraisers and keeping up with her six grandchildren, one of whom is getting married in two months.

I do my exercises religiously, I promise you that.
My neighbour, bless her heart, told me not to force it.
I just want to walk my granddaughter's wedding without that walker, is that so much to ask?
You're going to think I'm a terrible patient, aren't you?

Needing the walker at her granddaughter's wedding in two months
Being able to kneel in church again
Worry that bending the knee too much might damage the implant
Feeling like she might be seen as non-compliant or a bad patient

scenario.studentBrief: You are seeing Peggy O'Connell, a 74-year-old woman, for a telehealth physical therapy progress re-evaluation 6 weeks after a right total knee replacement. She was referred by orthopedic surgery for routine postoperative rehabilitation. Review the available chart, then conduct a focused interview and guided remote examination to assess her current status and update her plan of care.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Persistent right knee stiffness and limited bending 6 weeks after total knee replacement, with concern about falling behind the expected recovery timeline.
scenario.openingLine: My new knee just won't bend the way they told me it should by now, and I'm getting worried about it.
tasks: Take a focused history of her current function, pain, and home exercise program
Screen for postoperative complications via guided remote examination
Perform guided functional and range-of-motion measures appropriate for telehealth
Explore barriers to progress and reconcile self-report with available documentation
Establish patient-centered goals and agree on an updated plan of care

profile.summary: Peggy O'Connell is a 74-year-old woman seen by telehealth for a 6-week progress re-evaluation after right total knee arthroplasty, presenting with flexion stuck at 85 degrees, a 10-degree extension lag, and a Timed Up and Go of 22 seconds while still using a walker. The case teaches learners to reconcile self-reported exercise adherence with objective log data, uncover fear-avoidance beliefs driving avoidance of painful flexion exercises, screen for postoperative red flags remotely, and build a patient-centered plan of care tied to meaningful functional goals (an upcoming wedding, kneeling in church).
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in her living room in Buffalo, New York, with her walker nearby

answerKey.primaryProblem: Postoperative knee flexion and extension range-of-motion deficit (arthrofibrosis risk) 6 weeks after right total knee arthroplasty, compounded by fear-avoidance behavior and suboptimal home exercise adherence, resulting in delayed functional recovery (impaired gait, elevated Timed Up and Go, continued walker dependence).
differential: Expected but delayed postoperative stiffness due to inadequate therapeutic loading/adherence (most likely)
Arthrofibrosis requiring manipulation under anesthesia if ROM does not improve with intensified therapy
Postoperative infection (afebrile, healed incision, no drainage - against this)
Deep vein thrombosis (no calf tenderness/swelling/warmth - against this)
Component malposition or mechanical complication (would warrant surgeon referral if pain or ROM fails to progress despite adherent, well-dosed therapy)
keyFindings: Active knee flexion 85 degrees (surgeon goal 110-120 by 6 weeks)
Timed Up and Go 22 seconds (elevated, fall risk and functional limitation)
Objective exercise log shows adherence on only 9 of 28 days with no flexion exercises in 3 weeks, versus patient's report of daily religious adherence
Fear-avoidance belief reinforced by neighbour's advice not to 'force' the new knee
Nighttime pillow positioning under knee promoting extension contracture
Pain medication taken after rather than before exercise, limiting exercise tolerance
No signs of infection, DVT, or wound complication on remote screening
plan: Educate on normal postoperative healing timeline and the difference between expected discomfort with stretching versus harmful pain, directly addressing the fear that bending will damage the implant

Revise home exercise program to reinstate flexion-focused exercises (heel slides, wall slides, seated flexion overpressure) with clear dosing (frequency, hold times) and a return demonstration requirement at next visit
Prescribe extension-focused exercises/positioning (prone hangs, towel roll under ankle not knee) and instruct to discontinue the pillow-under-knee sleeping position
Counsel on premedication timing: take prescribed analgesic 30-45 minutes before exercise sessions rather than after, in coordination with prescribing provider
Address adherence using a structured daily log with simple tracking and short, achievable session targets to rebuild consistency
Progress functional training toward walker weaning with gait and balance exercises given elevated TUG, with clear criteria for safe progression

Set collaborative, meaningful functional goals: achieve full extension and at least 110-115 degrees flexion to allow efficient gait and stair use within 6-8 weeks, working toward unassisted ambulation for the wedding in 2 months

Schedule close interval follow-up (1-2 weeks) to reassess ROM trend and adherence; if flexion does not improve meaningfully despite adherent, well-dosed therapy over the next several weeks, refer back to orthopedic surgeon to evaluate for arthrofibrosis and possible manipulation under anesthesia
Continue surveillance for red flag signs (fever, increasing warmth/swelling, calf pain) and instruct patient to report these immediately
redFlags: Signs of surgical site infection: fever, increasing redness/warmth, purulent drainage - not present but should be monitored
Signs of DVT: calf pain, swelling, warmth, redness - not present but should be monitored

Failure of ROM to progress despite confirmed adherence and appropriate dosing over several more weeks, which would warrant referral back to the orthopedic surgeon for possible manipulation under anesthesia
New falls or near-falls given elevated Timed Up and Go, which would warrant falls risk reassessment
educationPoints: Postoperative knee stiffness after TKA is common and the window for regaining motion is time-sensitive; delaying aggressive bending exercises increases risk of permanent stiffness (arthrofibrosis)

Discomfort during therapeutic stretching that resolves quickly after stopping is expected and does not indicate the implant is being damaged; the implant is designed to tolerate full functional range of motion

Objective adherence tracking (not just self-report) is important for accurately interpreting slow progress and avoiding mislabeling a motivated patient as 'noncompliant' when the real issue is fear and lack of understanding
Positioning habits like sleeping with a pillow under the knee can passively reinforce a flexion contracture and should be replaced with extension-promoting positioning

Timing of PRN pain medication relative to exercise sessions can significantly affect a patient's ability to tolerate therapeutic stretching and should be optimized in coordination with the prescribing provider
Setting meaningful, patient-specific functional goals (e.g., a family wedding, kneeling in church) improves engagement and gives concrete targets for the plan of care

profile.title: 6-week post-TKA progress re-evaluation: knee stiffness and fear-avoidance limiting recovery in a 74-year-old woman
